digest.top_line: STAMPEDE: 2yr abiraterone on top of ADT+RT cuts metastasis risk nearly in half (MFS HR 0·53), 6-yr MFS 82% vs 69%; enzalutamide adds toxicity, not benefit.
digest.tldr: Prostate carried the day. In high-risk non-metastatic disease treated with ADT + 74 Gy/37 fx (85% planned for RT), 2yr abiraterone improves MFS HR 0·53 and OS HR 0·60, with no interaction by planned RT (p=0·67) or nodal status (p=0·22). Adding enzalutamide doubles G3+ toxicity (58% vs 37%) for no efficacy gain.

sites.intro: Intensifying the systemic arm around definitive RT, with the enzalutamide question answered in the negative.

studies.name: STAMPEDE (abiraterone ± enzalutamide, high-risk non-metastatic)
studies.tldr: MFS HR 0·53 (0·44–0·64), 6-yr MFS 82% vs 69%, adding 2yr abiraterone to ADT+RT; enzalutamide adds nothing.
details: 🔍 Two phase 3 trials in the STAMPEDE platform, 113 UK/Swiss sites, N=1974 non-metastatic, no overlapping controls, IPD meta-analysed
🔍 RT mandated for N0, encouraged for N+: 74 Gy/37 fx to prostate + SV or hypofractionated equivalent
🔍 1684 (85%) of 1974 planned for local RT; 99% of node-negative, 71% of node-positive newly diagnosed pts
📊 6-yr OS 86% combination vs 77% control; OS HR 0·60 (0·48–0·73), p<0·0001

details.text: 📊 Secondary endpoints, combination vs ADT alone (HR, 95% CI)

details: 📐 MFS by planned RT: RT yes HR 0·54 (0·44–0·67), RT no HR 0·51 (0·34–0·76), p-interaction 0·67
📐 MFS by nodal status: N0 HR 0·60 (0·46–0·78), N+ HR 0·49 (0·38–0·64), p-interaction 0·22
💊 Adding enzalutamide gave no extra efficacy: interaction HR 1·02 (0·70–1·50), p=0·91, I² p=0·90

details.text: ⚠️ Enzalutamide added toxicity without benefit (abi trial vs abi+enza trial, G3+)

details: ⚠️ Open label, and control pts could access 2nd-gen hormones in nmCRPC trials or, since 2019, as SOC
⚠️ Toxicity reported only for the first 24 months of treatment; late effects not captured
⚠️ MFS heterogeneity by WHO PS (p=0·00656) and NSAID/aspirin use (p=0·0052); authors call the latter biologically unexplained

verdict.rationale: Two prespecified randomised phase 3 trials, primary MFS endpoint hit with 72-mo median follow-up, OS concordant, in a population where RT plus ADT was the ceiling.
verdict.audience: High-risk non-metastatic prostate (N+ or 2 of T3-4/GS 8-10/PSA ≥40), or high-risk relapse

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is that 85% of pts were planned for radiotherapy (74 Gy/37 fx to prostate and SV, or hypofractionated equivalent), so this benefit sits on top of definitive local treatment, not instead of it. MFS gain held whether RT was planned or not (HR 0·54 vs 0·51, p-interaction 0·67), which moves the systemic intensification decision at the RT consult.
studies.monday_clinic: In high-risk node-positive or multi-feature node-negative disease starting long-course ADT with definitive prostate RT, this supports 2 years of abiraterone and prednisolone alongside; it does not extend to post-prostatectomy pts or the under-represented group relapsing after prior local therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Two open-label randomised phase 3 trials within the **STAMPEDE** MAMS platform, 113 UK and Swiss sites, same eligibility, **no overlapping controls**, pooled by IPD meta-analysis. Recruitment Nov 15, 2011 to March 31, 2016; median follow-up **72 months** (85 mo abiraterone trial, 60 mo abiraterone plus enzalutamide trial). Primary outcome was switched from OS to **metastasis-free survival** before any efficacy inspection, ratified by the independent trial steering committee.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **N=1974** non-metastatic pts: node positive, or node negative with **at least two of** T3-4, Gleason 8-10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL, or relapsing with high-risk features. Median age 68 (IQR 63-73), median PSA 34 ng/ml, **774 (39%) node positive**, 1563 (79%) of 1968 Gleason 8-10. WHO PS 0-2; clinically significant cardiovascular disease excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: ADT for **3 years** in all arms; abiraterone acetate 1000 mg with prednisolone 5 mg daily for **2 years**, plus enzalutamide 160 mg daily in the second trial. Median time to permanently stopping abiraterone was 23·7 months alone but **20·7 months in combination** with enzalutamide, and 23·2 months to stopping enzalutamide.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Local RT **mandated for node-negative** disease unless contraindicated and **encouraged for node-positive**, delivered per local guidelines at **74 Gy in 37 fractions** to prostate and seminal vesicles or a hypofractionated equivalent. Planned RT use was **1684 (85%) of 1974**, 99% of newly diagnosed node-negative pts, 71% of node-positive, and 7% of previously treated pts. Where RT was omitted, combination therapy could continue until progression rather than stopping at 2 years.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: metastasis-free survival.** Secondary: overall survival, prostate cancer-specific survival, biochemical failure-free survival, progression-free survival, toxicity. Powered at 90% with one-sided alpha 1·25% for a target MFS HR of 0·75, needing about 315 control-group events; 306 were observed in the control groups against 180 in the combination groups.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Effect was consistent across the two trials, MFS HR **0·54 (0·43-0·68)** in the abiraterone trial and **0·53 (0·39-0·71)** with enzalutamide added, with no between-trial heterogeneity. Proportional hazards held for MFS (p=0·46) and OS (p=0·10).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: G3+ events in the first 24 months: **169 (37%) of 451 vs 130 (29%) of 455** in the abiraterone trial, and **298 (58%) of 513 vs 172 (32%) of 533** with enzalutamide added. Hypertension and transaminitis drove the excess. Seven grade 5 events, **none in the control groups**: three on abiraterone plus prednisolone, four on the enzalutamide combination (two septic shock, two sudden death).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The abiraterone-in-metastatic STAMPEDE comparison and LATITUDE established second-generation hormone benefit in M1 disease; this extends it below the metastatic threshold, where **ADT plus RT alone** was the ceiling. The enzalutamide-added arm mirrors the mCRPC combination studies the authors cite, which showed **modest rPFS gain and no OS gain**, and reproduces that null here.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents newly diagnosed high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer staged by conventional imaging and treated with 3 years of ADT plus definitive prostate RT. Does not represent post-prostatectomy pts or pts relapsing after previous local therapy, both under-represented, and says nothing about an AR antagonist alone added to ADT and RT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Staging was by **conventional imaging** (bone scan, CT or MRI), so a PSMA-PET era cohort would migrate some of these pts to M1 and dilute the measured benefit. Data on subsequent therapy after castration resistance were judged unreliable, and the 2-year treatment duration was pragmatic, anchored to the ADT-with-RT requirement rather than tested.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The **enzalutamide result is the actionable negative**: an indirect comparison cannot exclude a small gain, but the doubled G3+ rate and the cost make it unjustified in this population. The NSAID/aspirin heterogeneity (p=0·0052) has no biological explanation and the authors state it should not affect management.

studies.interpretation:
The value of this report is not that hormone intensification works in prostate cancer, which was already established in the metastatic setting, but that it works on top of a genuinely modern local backbone. Eighty-five percent of these pts were planned for radiotherapy at 74 Gy in 37 fractions or a hypofractionated equivalent, with three years of ADT, which was the ceiling of care for high-risk non-metastatic disease at the time. An intervention that halves metastasis-free survival events against that comparator is doing more than an intervention that improves on ADT alone, and the OS HR of 0·60 with 6-year survival 86% versus 77% says the MFS gain is not a pure surrogate artefact. That concordance matters, because MFS became the primary endpoint by a mid-trial change; the change was made and independently ratified before any efficacy data were inspected, and the OS result independently supports the same conclusion, so the substitution is defensible rather than opportunistic.

The two-trial structure is the strongest design feature here and is easy to undersell. These were not one trial split post hoc. They were separately randomised with separately accrued, non-overlapping control groups in different calendar periods, and they reproduced each other almost exactly, 0·54 versus 0·53 for MFS. A single trial of this size gives you one estimate with one set of era-specific confounders; two give you an internal replication, which is why the pooled estimate should carry more weight than its sample size alone suggests.

For a radiation oncologist the question is whether the benefit is additive to RT or partly substitutes for it, and the trial cannot fully answer that because RT was not randomised. What it does give is a prespecified subgroup by planned RT, and the estimates are indistinguishable, 0·54 with planned RT and 0·51 without, interaction p=0·67. The RT-free stratum is small (145 per group) and the protocol allowed combination therapy to run past two years when RT was omitted, so the two subgroups are not treated identically and the comparison should not be pushed hard. The honest read is that nothing here suggests the systemic benefit is contingent on local treatment or vice versa, and the practical implication is that a pt being consented for definitive prostate RT with long-course ADT should also be having the abiraterone conversation.

The enzalutamide comparison is the cleanly negative half and is arguably the more immediately useful result. It is an indirect comparison across trials rather than a head-to-head, so it cannot exclude a small increment, but the interaction HR of 1·02 with a confidence interval spanning 0·70 to 1·50 sits over a doubling of grade 3 or worse events, 58% against 37%, and four of the seven grade 5 events on trial. The authors anticipated this null from the mCRPC combination data before unblinding, which makes it a confirmed prediction rather than a surprise, and the conclusion that the added cost and toxicity are unjustified is well supported.

What would make this estimate wrong, or at least smaller, in 2026 practice is staging. Eligibility rested on conventional imaging, so a fraction of this population would be reclassified as metastatic on PSMA-PET today, and those pts plausibly contributed disproportionately to the events prevented. Applying the HR unchanged to a PET-staged, genuinely node-negative high-risk cohort risks overestimating absolute benefit. The other real boundary is the post-prostatectomy pt and the pt relapsing after prior local therapy, both explicitly under-represented and left unresolved by the authors.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 85% of pts were planned for RT (74 Gy/37 fx to prostate and SV, or hypofractionated equivalent), so the benefit is additive to definitive local treatment rather than a substitute. MFS gain held with and without planned RT (HR 0·54 vs 0·51, p-interaction 0·67), so raise abiraterone at the RT consult alongside 3 years of ADT.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The enzalutamide arm is the decision: adding it to abiraterone gave interaction HR 1·02 (0·70–1·50) for MFS while G3+ events went from 37% to 58%, so doublet AR blockade is not justified here. Two years of abiraterone with prednisolone on 3 years of ADT is the regimen that carries the OS HR 0·60.
